New palaeomagnetic data from Argun terrane. Testing its association
with Amuria and the Mongol–Okhotsk Ocean
I.V. Gordienko,1 D.V. Меtеlkin,2,3 L.I. Vetluzhskikh,1 N.E. Mikhaltsov2,3
and E.V. Kulakov4
1GeologicalInstitute,SBRAS,Sakhyanovast.6a,Ulan-Ude670047,Russia
2NovosibirskStateUniversity,Pirogovast.1,Novosibirsk630090,Russia.E-mail:metelkindv@ipgg.sbras.ru
3TrofimukInstituteofPetroleumGeologyandGeophysics,SBRAS,Koptugaave.,3,Novosibirsk630090,Russia
4TheCenterforEarthEvolutionandDynamics,UniversityofOslo,Postboks1028Blindern0316OSLO,Norway
Accepted2018February9.Received2018January28;inoriginalform2017April20
SUMMARY
Inthisstudy,wepresentnewpalaeomagneticandgeologicaldataobtainedfromEdiacaranand
CambriansedimentaryrocksofArgunterrane,whichistraditionallyconsideredakeyelement
ofthehypotheticalAmuriacompositecontinent.Since1990,whenAmuriawasfirstproposed
in palaeogeographic reconstructions, it became one of the principle members in the global
palaeotectonicschemes.AscenariowhencollisionofAmuriawithSiberianmarginresulted
informationoftheMongol–OkhotskOceanisuniversallyacceptedandsupportedbymajority
ofresearchers.However,timeofAmuria’sfinalassemblyandrelativepositionoftheblocks
within Amuria before the collision with Siberia is still a topic of debate. Questions about
principalallocationofArgunterraneanditsrelationtoAmuriaduringthelateNeoroterozoic–
Cambrianareaddressedinthisstudy.PalaeomagneticpolesfortheEdiacaran–earlyCambrian
rocks of Argun terrane differ within an error from coeval poles from Siberia indicating that
Argunterranecouldhavebeenlocatedsimilartoitspresent-daypositionwithrespecttoSiberia
alreadyat560–525Ma.ThisobservationcallsintoquestionassociationofArgunterranewith
Amuria, which in classic reconstructions is usually placed close to the North China Craton.
ItalsoquestionsourcurrentunderstandingoftheAmuriapalaeocontinentandconsequently,
accuracyofglobalpalaeogeographicreconstructionsforthelateNeoproterozoic–Cambrianin
general,andthoseoftheeasternpartoftheCentralAsiainparticular.

gent;Continentaltectonics;Cratons.

3.2 Methodsandequipment
Palaeomagneticandrock-magneticanalyseshavebeenconducted
according to the standard techniques using instruments available
in the Paleomagnetic Center of the Institute of Petroleum Geol-
ogyandGeophysicsSBRAS,Novosibirsk.Magneticmineralogy
was examined using an AGICO MFK1-FA magnetic susceptibil-
itymeterequippedwithahigh-temperaturefurnace.Temperature
dependencesoflow-fieldmagneticsusceptibility,κ(T),weremea-
sured upon cycling from room temperature to 700 ◦C (in argon)
with subsequent cooling to the room temperature. For the major-
ity of measured powders, the κ(T) curves were irreversible and
revealedlaboratory-inducedalterationofmagneticmineralsupon
heatingover350◦С,resultinginneoformationofamagneticphase
with Curie temperatures typical for magnetite. According to this
result, alternating field (AF) demagnetization was considered an
optimalmagneticcleaningprotocolforoursamples.Magneticre-
manencewasmeasuredwitha2GEnterprises755superconduct-
ingrockmagnetometerequippedwithanAFdemagnetizingunit.
Aftermeasurementofanaturalremanentmagnetization(NRM),AF
stepwisedemagnetizationtothefieldupto140mTwasperformed
onspecimenspreparedfromeachcoresample.DirectionsofNRM
componentsweredeterminedusingpalaeomagneticsoftwarewith
built-inanalyticaltoolsforprincipalcomponentandgreatremagne-
tizationcirclesanalyses(Kirschvink1980;McFadden&McElhinny
1988).Differentmodificationsofthefoldtestwereutilizedinor-
dertotesttheageofcharacteristiccomponentofNRM(McFadden
1990;Watson&Enkin1993;Enkin2003).
3.3 Beletuyformation
NRM intensities and quality of palaeomagnetic signal are vari-
able in samples from different rock units. The sandstones typi-
callydisplayrelativelyhighNRMvaluesinarangeof10−2–10−1
Аm−1.Thermomagneticcurvesforthesesamplesappearedsome-
whatnoisy.CharacteristicCurie(Neel)temperaturesforthemain
magnetic minerals were difficult to determine precisely. Heating
cycles are characterized by a drop in magnetic susceptibility at
320◦С,indicativeforthepresenceofpyrrhotite(Fig.6a).Greater
valuesofmagneticsusceptibilityduringthecoolingleg(oncooling
from∼500◦С)suggestformationofanewmagneticphase(proba-
blymagnetite)duetoheating-inducedtransformationofpyrrhotite
(e.g.Dekkers1990)and/orreductionofhaematiteintoacubicfer-
romagnetic phase (similar to magnetite). The sandstones as well
asdolomitesrevealedsignificantlynon-uniformbehaviourduring
AF demagnetization. The median destructive field (MDF) val-
ues vary from 5 to 40 mT. Palaeomagnetic signal is not stable,
